title: Cloaking Cosmic Light
summary: Light crossing dark domain walls that source a top form coupled to gauge Chern--Simons terms mixing visible and dark $U(1)$ gauge fields generically converts into dark photons. The effect is entirely localized on the wall and requires no additional ingredients. The conversion rate is a sharp function of the photon frequency in the wall rest frame, vanishing above the ultraviolet cutoff of the top form sector. Partial cloaking may also induce a rotation of the polarization of transmitted light of order $Δ\vartheta \sim 10^{-3}$ radians, modify the cosmic microwave background power spectrum, and violate Etherington's reciprocity relation at low frequencies. These effects can impact cosmological determinations of the Hubble rate.

AI.tldr: Light crossing dark domain walls can convert into dark photons, rotating polarization and modifying cosmological observables, potentially impacting Hubble rate measurements.
AI.motivation: To explore novel physical effects arising from dark domain walls coupled through top forms and gauge Chern--Simons terms, particularly the conversion of photons into dark photons and their cosmological consequences, which could impact precision measurements like the Hubble rate.
AI.method: The paper analyzes the coupling of top forms to gauge Chern--Simons terms mixing visible and dark U(1) gauge fields, modeling the interaction of light crossing dark domain walls, and computes the frequency-dependent conversion rate to dark photons along with induced polarization rotation and cosmological implications such as modifications to the cosmic microwave background and Etherington's relation.
AI.result: The paper studies the interaction between light and dark domain walls sourced by a top form coupled to gauge Chern--Simons terms involving visible and dark U(1) gauge fields. It shows that light crossing such domain walls can convert into dark photons, a process localized on the wall and dependent on photon frequency with a cutoff above the top form sector's ultraviolet scale. This mechanism can also rotate the polarization of light, alter the cosmic microwave background power spectrum, and cause deviations from Etherington's reciprocity relation, potentially affecting cosmological measurements such as the Hubble parameter determination.
AI.conclusion: The conversion of photons into dark photons upon crossing dark domain walls sourced by top forms coupled to gauge Chern--Simons terms is a localized, frequency-dependent effect that can induce measurable polarization rotation, modify cosmological observables like the CMB power spectrum, and affect cosmological distance relations, thus influencing determinations of the Hubble rate.

title: Cosmological Constraints on Neutrino Masses in Quintessential Inflation
summary: Quintessential inflation provides a unified description of the early and late accelerated phases of the Universe, linking the inflationary epoch to the present-day dark energy-dominated era through a single scalar degree of freedom. In this work, we explore the implications of this unification for cosmological constraints on the sum of neutrino masses. Focusing on the $α$-attractor scenario, we implement the model in a modified version of the Boltzmann solver CLASS to compute the relevant cosmological observables and perform a Bayesian parameter estimation analysis using data from the cosmic microwave background (CMB), baryon acoustic oscillations (BAOs), and Type Ia supernovae. The model naturally breaks the degeneracy between the dark energy equation of state and the total neutrino mass, yielding tight upper bounds of $\sum m_ν< 0.067$ eV for flat spatial geometry and $\sum m_ν< 0.116$ eV when curvature is included. We also provide forecasts for future probes, showing that the Simons Observatory, LiteBIRD, and Euclid configurations may reduce the uncertainty on $\sum m_ν$ by $\approx 9\%$, while the precision on the quintessential parameter $α_{QI}$ is improved by $\approx 72\%$. These results highlight the importance of consistently accounting for neutrino mass when assessing the viability of extensions to the standard cosmological model.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates quintessential inflation within the α-attractor framework to unify early and late cosmic acceleration phases, analyzing its impact on neutrino mass constraints using cosmological data. It breaks degeneracies between dark energy and neutrino mass, providing tight upper bounds and forecasting improved parameter precision with future observatories.
AI.motivation: To unify the early inflationary and late-time accelerated cosmic expansion epochs via a single scalar field model and to explore how this unification influences constraints on the total neutrino mass in cosmology.
AI.method: The authors implement the α-attractor quintessential inflation model in the CLASS Boltzmann solver, computing cosmological observables. They employ Bayesian parameter estimation using CMB, BAO, and Type Ia supernovae data, and perform forecasts for future experiments like Simons Observatory, LiteBIRD, and Euclid.
AI.result: The model yields upper limits on the sum of neutrino masses of <0.067 eV (flat geometry) and <0.116 eV (with curvature). Forecasts predict a ~9% reduction in neutrino mass uncertainty and a ~72% improvement in the quintessential parameter α precision with upcoming cosmological surveys.
AI.conclusion: Quintessential inflation models tightly constrain the sum of neutrino masses, breaking degeneracies with dark energy parameters, and future observational probes are expected to enhance the precision of both neutrino mass and quintessential inflation parameters.

title: IR-Safe and IR-Resummed Bispectra Before and After Reconstruction in Unified Lagrangian Perturbation Theory
summary: We develop a unified analytic framework for modeling the real-space dark matter bispectrum, including both auto and cross bispectra constructed from pre- and post-reconstruction density fields, based on Unified Lagrangian Perturbation Theory (ULPT). ULPT reorganizes the standard Lagrangian approach by separating the Jacobian deviation, which generates the nonlinear source bispectrum, from the displacement-mapping effect that determines how long-wavelength bulk flows distort observed configurations. Within this structure, we derive general one-loop ULPT expressions for the bispectrum and analyze their infrared (IR) behavior, demonstrating exact, nonperturbative IR cancellation and the natural emergence of an IR-resummed description of baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) damping. In particular, ULPT enables a detailed and fully analytic treatment of the wiggle-wiggle contribution to the IR-resummed bispectrum, whose structure has remained comparatively unexplored in previous approaches. We further construct IR-resummed models for the cross bispectra of all pre- and post-reconstruction combinations. For configurations in which the displacement fields differ, ULPT captures not only the overall exponential damping but also the more intricate BAO-scale modulation characteristic of mixed pre/post bispectra. Our results clarify the physical origin of nonlinear BAO suppression and provide a compact theoretical framework in which the full ULPT bispectrum, once implemented numerically through displacement-mapping convolution integrals, will automatically encode all nonlinear BAO and IR effects. The framework developed here therefore offers a unified and IR-safe foundation for interpreting next-generation bispectrum measurements.

AI.tldr: This study develops a ULPT-based framework for modeling dark matter bispectra, incorporating IR cancellations and BAO damping with analytic precision, enabling robust interpretation of future cosmological measurements.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to build a comprehensive and unified analytic model for the real-space dark matter bispectrum that can accurately describe nonlinear effects, infrared behavior, and BAO damping, thereby improving theoretical interpretation and analysis of upcoming precise bispectrum measurements in cosmology.
AI.method: The method involves reorganizing the Lagrangian perturbative expansion by isolating the Jacobian deviation and displacement-mapping effects, deriving general one-loop ULPT bispectrum expressions, and performing analytic IR behavior analysis leading to exact IR cancellations and IR-resummed BAO damping. It constructs IR-resummed models for all pre/post-reconstruction bispectrum combinations and implements displacement-mapping convolution integrals for numerical evaluation.
AI.result: The paper presents a unified analytic framework based on Unified Lagrangian Perturbation Theory (ULPT) to model the real-space dark matter bispectrum, including auto- and cross bispectra from pre- and post-reconstruction density fields. It reorganizes the standard Lagrangian approach by separating nonlinear source terms from displacement effects, derives one-loop bispectrum expressions, and demonstrates exact infrared (IR) cancellations and IR-resummed baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) damping. The approach enables analytic treatment of the previously unexplored wiggle-wiggle contributions, accurately models cross bispectra of various reconstruction states, and captures both exponential damping and BAO-scale modulations. This clarifies the physical origin of nonlinear BAO suppression and provides an IR-safe theoretical framework for interpreting future bispectrum data.
AI.conclusion: ULPT provides a unified, IR-safe analytic methodology that captures nonlinear BAO suppression and displacement effects in bispectra, offering a compact theoretical foundation for next-generation bispectrum analyses.

title: Machine-learning cosmological parameters by eROSITA data
comment: Submitted, 15 pages and 12 figures. Comments are welcome!
summary: Context: We present the first Cosmological Parameter inferences from eROSITA X-ray observations of galaxy clusters using a Machine Learning algorithm. Methods: We train a Random Forest using mock catalogs of clusters from Magneticum multi-cosmology hydrodynamical simulations. We apply the trained ML algorithm to observed X-ray features (gas luminosity, mass, and temperature) at different redshifts from the eROSITA eFEDS and eRASS1 catalogs. Results: We obtain cosmological constraints with precision comparable to those from standard analyses, such as weak lensing and cluster abundances. We infer $Ω_{\rm m}=0.30^{+0.03}_{-0.02}$, $σ_8=0.81\pm0.01$, and $h_0=0.710\pm0.004$. The recovered parameters show no tension in the $Ω_{\rm m}-σ_8$ space, but a significant deviation of $h_0$ from the Planck estimates. These inferences remain rather stable against variations of the input observable set and parameter space coverage. These results indicate that correlations among intracluster properties contain cosmological information beyond that encoded in the cluster abundance alone, which can be captured by machine learning trained on multi-cosmology simulations. Conclusions: ML algorithms trained on multi-cosmology hydrodynamical simulations can effectively infer cosmological parameters directly from galaxy cluster data. This is a change of paradigm in the context of cosmological parameter inferences. This approach complements traditional cluster-count analyses and is particularly suited to large upcoming surveys, where systematic uncertainties in mass calibration may otherwise dominate the error budget. It also highlights the potential of large-scale X-ray surveys to deliver independent tests of the standard cosmological model.

AI.tldr: Machine learning trained on hydrodynamical simulations infers cosmological parameters from eROSITA galaxy clusters with precision comparable to standard methods, offering an innovative complementary approach for cosmology.
AI.motivation: Current cosmological parameter inference methods from galaxy clusters rely heavily on cluster abundance and suffer from systematic errors like mass calibration. Leveraging machine learning on simulations that include multi-cosmology scenarios enables capturing additional cosmological information embedded in correlations between intracluster properties, improving inference robustness and precision.
AI.method: A Random Forest algorithm was trained on mock galaxy cluster catalogs derived from Magneticum multi-cosmology hydrodynamical simulations. The trained model was applied to X-ray observables such as gas luminosity, mass, and temperature at various redshifts from the eROSITA eFEDS and eRASS1 surveys to infer cosmological parameters.
AI.result: This paper presents a novel approach for inferring cosmological parameters using machine learning (Random Forest) trained on hydrodynamical simulations, applied to eROSITA X-ray observed galaxy cluster data. This method achieves precision comparable to traditional techniques and reveals new cosmological information from intracluster property correlations beyond mere cluster counts.
AI.conclusion: ML algorithms trained on multi-cosmology hydrodynamical simulations provide effective and reliable estimates of cosmological parameters directly from cluster data, representing a paradigm shift and complementing traditional cluster-count analyses while mitigating mass calibration systematics.

title: High Resolution VLA Radio Observations of the Boomerang Pulsar Wind Nebula
summary: We present a radio polarimetric study of the Boomerang pulsar wind nebula G106.65+2.96 with VLA observations at the 6 GHz band. Our high-resolution image discovers new small-scale features in the nebula, including an elliptical core of $40''\times20''$ surrounding the central pulsar and a $2'$-long arc wrapping around the core in the north. The latter shows a clear gap from the core, and it consists of a bright lobe in the northwest and a tongue-like structure in the northeast. These could be resulting from the pulsar wind interaction with the environment. Our polarization measurement reveals a highly ordered magnetic field with toroidal geometry. The small scale features are all highly linearly polarized. In particular, the lobe has a polarization fraction of $\sim$60%, close to the synchrotron limit. This is also much higher than the value measured at a lower frequency, implying significant depolarization. We show that this can be explained by Faraday rotation in the nebula, and we constructed a simple 3D model accordingly to infer a magnetic field strength of $\sim$50-105$μ$G.

AI.tldr: High-resolution radio polarimetry of the Boomerang pulsar wind nebula uncovers new small-scale structures with highly ordered toroidal magnetic fields and very high polarization fractions, explained by Faraday rotation effects, yielding a magnetic field estimate of 50–105 μG.
AI.motivation: To achieve a detailed understanding of the magnetic field structure and small-scale morphological features of the Boomerang pulsar wind nebula, and to explain observed polarization discrepancies by modeling Faraday rotation effects in order to quantify the nebula's magnetic field strength.
AI.method: High-resolution VLA observations at 6 GHz produced detailed radio polarimetric imaging of the nebula. Measurements of linear polarization and comparison with lower-frequency data enabled assessment of depolarization effects due to Faraday rotation. A simple 3D magnetic field model was constructed to interpret the polarization data and infer magnetic field strength.
AI.result: The paper presents high-resolution 6 GHz VLA radio polarimetric observations of the Boomerang pulsar wind nebula G106.65+2.96, revealing previously unknown small-scale features such as an elliptical core around the pulsar and an arc structure to the north. These structures likely arise from interactions between the pulsar wind and its environment. Polarization data show a highly ordered toroidal magnetic field and unusually high linear polarization (up to ~60%), indicating minimal depolarization at high frequencies. The discrepancy from lower-frequency polarization is attributed to Faraday rotation within the nebula. A simple 3D model is developed to estimate the nebular magnetic field strength as approximately 50–105 microgauss.
AI.conclusion: The Boomerang pulsar wind nebula exhibits complex small-scale morphology and a highly ordered toroidal magnetic field with significant Faraday depolarization at lower frequencies. The estimated magnetic field strength is in the range of 50–105 μG, derived from a 3D model fitting polarization data.

title: Bypassing the Lyth Bound with Entangled Gravitons: Primordial Signatures and Late-Time Noise
summary: We demonstrate that quantum entanglement between primordial gravitons in dynamically decoupled gravitational sectors can parametrically enhance the tensor power spectrum during inflation. Unlike standard mechanisms relying on classical dynamics or modified actions, this enhancement originates from the reduced density matrix of the observable sector after tracing over a hidden gravitational reservoir. This framework allows for a sizable tensor-to-scalar ratio r > 0.01 consistent with sub-Planckian inflaton excursions, providing a purely quantum mechanical evasion of the Lyth bound. The resulting mixed state leaves a distinctive "quantum birthmark" in the form of oscillatory features in the power spectrum and a characteristic violation of the single-field consistency relation, manifesting as a scale-dependent enhancement of the squeezed-limit bispectrum. Furthermore, we forecast that this entanglement may manifest as a late-time stochastic noise enhancement in gravitational wave interferometers, offering a novel experimental window into the quantum nature of spacetime.

AI.tldr: Quantum entanglement between hidden and observable gravitons can increase the tensor power spectrum during inflation, producing detectable signatures like oscillations and bispectrum anomalies while circumventing classical constraints on inflation models.
AI.motivation: To explain how quantum entanglement effects during inflation can enhance primordial gravitational wave signatures beyond classical limits, enabling sub-Planckian inflationary models to evade the Lyth bound and provide unique observational predictions.
AI.method: The study analyzes the reduced density matrix of the observable gravitational sector by tracing out a hidden gravitational reservoir, modeling the quantum entanglement between separated gravitational sectors and its impact on the inflationary tensor power spectrum and higher-order correlators.
AI.result: The paper presents a novel quantum mechanical mechanism where entanglement between primordial gravitons in separate gravitational sectors enhances the tensor power spectrum during inflation. This occurs through the reduced density matrix obtained after tracing out a hidden gravitational reservoir, leading to a large tensor-to-scalar ratio without requiring large inflaton field excursions, thus evading the traditional Lyth bound. Observable consequences include oscillatory features in the power spectrum, violation of single-field inflation consistency relations, scale-dependent squeezed-limit bispectrum enhancements, and potential late-time stochastic noise detectable by gravitational wave interferometers.
AI.conclusion: Quantum entanglement in gravitational sectors can yield a sizable tensor-to-scalar ratio and distinct observational signatures, offering a new quantum-origin perspective on primordial gravitational waves and promising experimental probes via gravitational wave detectors.

title: The origin of isolated millisecond pulsars in globular clusters
summary: A significant fraction of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) in globular clusters (GCs) are observed as isolated objects, despite the widely accepted scenario in which MSPs are formed through recycling in compact binary systems. The origin of these isolated objects therefore remains an open problem. In this Letter, we propose a physically motivated encounter rate per binary, $Λ\propto n a/(σa_H)$, incorporating the local stellar density $n$, velocity dispersion $σ$, binary separation $a$, and the Heggie--Hills ionization radius $a_H$. Combined with companion ablation by the MSP, this rate successfully predicts the observed fraction of isolated MSPs in GCs, that is $\mathcal{F}_i \proptoΛ\propto a_H^{-1}$, establishing dynamical ionization as the primary channel for producing isolated MSPs. We quantitatively test this model against a null hypothesis in which $\mathcal{F}_i$ is independent of $a_H$, and find that the ionization-driven model is 220 times more likely than the null hypothesis. Our framework naturally explains the observed overabundance of isolated MSPs in $ω$ Centauri and establishes binary ionization as the primary mechanism responsible for the production of isolated MSPs in GCs.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the puzzle of isolated millisecond pulsars (MSPs) in globular clusters, proposing a dynamical ionization model based on encounter rates and binary properties to explain their origin.
AI.motivation: To explain the origin of isolated millisecond pulsars in globular clusters, which remain puzzling since MSPs are believed to form in binary systems.
AI.method: The authors introduced a physically motivated encounter rate per binary considering local stellar density, velocity dispersion, binary separation, and the Heggie-Hills ionization radius. They combined this with companion ablation effects by MSPs, and statistically tested their model against a null hypothesis independent of ionization radius effects.
AI.result: The model predicts isolated MSP fractions proportional to the inverse ionization radius, fitting observational data well and showing the model to be 220 times more likely than a null hypothesis. The framework also explains the overabundance of isolated MSPs in ω Centauri.
AI.conclusion: Dynamical ionization driven by stellar encounters is the primary mechanism producing isolated MSPs in globular clusters, successfully matching observed isolated MSP fractions.

title: Cylindrical cosmological simulations with StePS
summary: The global topology of the Universe can affect the long-range gravitational forces through the boundary conditions. To study non-trivial topologies in detail, simulations that natively adopt such geometries are required. Cosmological $N$-body simulations typically evolve matter in a periodic cubic box. While numerically convenient, this imposes a non-trivial 3-torus topology that affects long-range gravitational forces, potentially biasing large-scale statistics. We introduce a compactified simulation framework that is only periodic along a single axis, while having infinite topology with isotropic boundary conditions towards the perpendicular directions, i.e. an $\mathrm{S}^1\times\mathbb{R}^2$ ("slab") topology. This new simulation geometry is ideal for simulating systems with cylindrical symmetries like filaments or certain anisotropic cosmological models. We compactify comoving space via inverse stereographic projection along the radial direction of a periodic cylinder, and evolve particles with Newtonian dynamics. A smoothly varying spatial and mass resolution with radius suppresses edge artefacts at the free outer boundary. Our implementation in the StePS (STEreographically Projected cosmological Simulations) framework uses a direct $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ force calculation that maps efficiently to GPUs, and Octree $\mathcal{O}(N \log N)$ force calculation that can be used on large CPU-clusters. The cylindrical domain's topology enables fully self-consistent simulations in the $\mathrm{S}^1\times\mathbb{R}^2$ manifold and mitigates periodic-image artefacts for targets whose symmetries are mismatched to a cubic box. The main trade-off is radially varying resolution with distinct systematics and analysis requirements. We demonstrate the accuracy of the new simulation method in a standard $Λ$CDM cosmological simulation.

AI.tldr: A new cosmological N-body simulation method uses a slab topology with one periodic axis to better model cylindrical symmetries and anisotropic systems, reducing biases from cubic periodic boxes and demonstrating accurate results in ΛCDM scenarios.
AI.motivation: Traditional cosmological N-body simulations use periodic cubic boxes imposing a 3-torus topology, which biases long-range gravitational forces and large-scale statistics for non-trivial topologies and anisotropic systems.
AI.method: They introduce a compactified simulation framework with a slab topology (S^1 x R^2), periodic along one axis and infinite with isotropic boundary conditions in perpendicular directions, using inverse stereographic projection and Newtonian dynamics, implemented in the StePS framework with direct O(N^2) and Octree O(N log N) force calculations optimized for GPUs and CPU clusters.
AI.result: The new slab topology simulation accurately captures cylindrical symmetries and anisotropic cosmological models, reduces periodic-image artifacts seen in cubic boxes, and demonstrates reliable performance in standard ΛCDM cosmological simulations, albeit with radially varying resolution and distinct systematics.
AI.conclusion: The compactified S^1 x R^2 simulation framework provides a valuable alternative to cubic-box simulations, enabling more accurate and self-consistent modeling of cosmological structures with cylindrical symmetry and non-trivial topologies, thereby mitigating biases inherent in traditional periodic cubic simulations.

title: Galactic Center Gamma-Ray Excess from a Generic Triaxial Halo
summary: Recent studies of Galactic surveys, such as Gaia, have revealed that the Milky Way's gravitational potential comes from a matter distribution that is triaxial and rotated with respect to the Galactic center-Sun axis. This, in turn, could mean that the dark matter halo also shares these properties. In this work, by fitting to the Fermi-LAT gamma-ray observations, we test the compatibility of the morphology of the Galactic Center Excess (GCE) from dark matter annihilation with a triaxial dark matter halo. In particular, we consider both untilted triaxial halos and halos whose principal axes are tilted with respect to the Galactic disk. In our fits of the Fermi-LAT data, by testing over a large library of galactic diffuse emission models, we quantify how the halo triaxiality and tilt affect the line-of-sight-integrated annihilation signal and, consequently, the preferred GCE spatial templates. We find that the GCE spectrum and inner cuspiness are robust against variations in the triaxiality and tilt of the dark matter halo. However, in terms of its overall morphology, the GCE in the gamma-ray data can discriminate between choices for the dark matter halo's triaxiality and tilt. Finally, we find that the GCE is more compatible with originating from a triaxial and tilted halo of dark matter than originating from a triaxial and tilted halo of stars, a result important for understanding the GCE's origin.

AI.tldr: This study tests the Galactic Center Excess gamma-ray signal against triaxial and tilted dark matter halo models, finding that the morphology of the excess favours a dark matter origin with a triaxial and tilted halo configuration.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether the morphology of the Galactic Center Excess (GCE) seen in gamma rays is consistent with a triaxial and possibly tilted dark matter halo, motivated by recent Galactic surveys indicating a triaxial and rotated gravitational potential of the Milky Way.
AI.method: Fitting Fermi-LAT gamma-ray observations using models of triaxial dark matter halos, including untilted and tilted configurations relative to the Galactic disk, and testing across a large library of galactic diffuse emission models.
AI.result: The GCE spectrum and inner cuspiness remain stable regardless of halo triaxiality and tilt, but the GCE morphology in gamma-ray data can discern differences in halo triaxiality and tilt. The GCE is found to be more consistent with a triaxial and tilted dark matter halo than with a similarly structured stellar halo.
AI.conclusion: The Galactic Center Excess morphology supports the hypothesis that it originates from annihilation in a triaxial and tilted dark matter halo rather than a triaxial and tilted stellar halo, providing insight into the nature of the GCE and the shape of the Milky Way’s dark matter distribution.

title: Constraints on CMBR flux due to high-z dust emission
comment: 3 pages, accepted for publication in Research Notes of the AAS
summary: Gjergo & Kroupa (2025) have proposed a new foreground CMBR component produced by dust associated with the progenitor clouds at $z=15-20$ that led to the formation of massive early-type galaxies, calculating that a minimum of 1.4% and a maximum of 100% of the whole CMBR radiation would be produced by this mechanism. Here, I check how much dust emission is compatible with the spectrum of the CMBR monopole flux measurements within the corresponding errors. COBE-FIRAS monopole is fitted to different models with different dust emissivity spectral indexes ($β$) and dispersion of redshifts of the progenitor clouds ($σ_d$). Within the realistic values of $β\ge 0.5$, $σ_d\ge 0.8$, the contamination of CMBR flux by high $z$ dust should be $<1.3$% (95% CL).

AI.tldr: The study constrains dust emission from early universe progenitor clouds to less than 1.3% contamination of the CMBR monopole flux, based on COBE-FIRAS data and realistic dust parameters.
AI.motivation: To test and quantify the proposed contribution of dust emission from early universe progenitor clouds to the CMBR monopole flux, and to assess if this mechanism can explain a significant fraction of the observed CMBR radiation.
AI.method: COBE-FIRAS monopole flux measurements were fitted to models incorporating various dust emissivity spectral indexes (β) and dispersions of progenitor cloud redshifts (σ_d), evaluating the compatibility of dust emission contamination within observational errors.
AI.result: The paper evaluates the contribution of dust emission from high redshift (z=15-20) progenitor clouds, as proposed by Gjergo & Kroupa (2025), to the Cosmic Microwave Background Radiation (CMBR) monopole flux. Using COBE-FIRAS data, different dust emissivity spectral indexes (β) and redshift dispersion parameters (σ_d) are modeled to constrain dust contamination. The analysis finds that for realistic parameter values (β≥0.5 and σ_d≥0.8), the dust contribution to the CMBR flux is limited to less than 1.3% at 95% confidence level, which is significantly lower than the maximum 100% suggested previously.
AI.conclusion: Dust contamination of the CMBR monopole flux from high redshift progenitor clouds is tightly limited to below 1.3% at 95% confidence, indicating that large fractions of CMBR from this dust component are incompatible with current measurements.

title: Introduction to Strong Alfvénic MHD Turbulence
comment: 34 pages, 13 figures; This is the submitted version prior to formal peer review. The accepted version has more contents and is available at Review of Modern Plasma Physics' website; see https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s41614-026-00214-0
summary: Many astrophysical fluids are magnetized and turbulent. Such fluids can be often described by magnetohydrodynamics (MHD). In this review, we mainly consider MHD turbulence with a strong mean magnetic field whose energy density is greater than or equal to the local kinetic energy density. In these fluids, the MHD waves, especially Alfvén waves, play a dominant dynamical role. Alfvén waves travel along magnetic field lines and collisions of opposite-traveling Alfvén wave packets are essential for turbulence cascade. We focus on strong turbulence regime, where nonlinear interaction during the collision is sufficiently strong and thus one collision is enough to complete turbulence cascade. We will cover the following types of turbulence. First, we review strong Alfvénic MHD turbulence. If the mean magnetic field is very strong, wave packets move very fast and duration of collision is too short to complete turbulence cascade. Even in this case we will show that strong turbulence regime emerges on a small scale. Second, we will consider small-scale MHD turbulence, where interaction of small-scale variants of Alfvén waves (i.e., whistler waves) is important. Third, we review scaling relations in strong relativistic force-free MHD turbulence, where interaction of relativistic Alfvén waves is important. Finally, we briefly discuss scaling relations in compressible MHD turbulence, where interaction of Alfvén waves is still important.

AI.tldr: This review examines how Alfvén wave interactions drive strong turbulence cascades in magnetized astrophysical fluids, covering strong Alfvénic turbulence, small-scale whistler turbulence, relativistic force-free turbulence, and compressible MHD turbulence, highlighting universal scaling behaviors.
AI.motivation: To provide a comprehensive review and understanding of the dynamics and scaling relations of various regimes of magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence in astrophysical fluids with strong mean magnetic fields, focusing on the role of Alfvén waves in turbulence cascade.
AI.method: The authors systematically review and synthesize previous theoretical and observational research on MHD turbulence with strong mean magnetic fields, focusing on the dominant role of Alfvén and related wave dynamics in multiple turbulence regimes, supported by scaling relation analyses.
AI.result: The study highlights that in strong mean magnetic fields, Alfvén waves dominate the turbulent dynamics and the cascade process is completed after a single strong nonlinear collision in the strong turbulence regime. It shows the emergence of strong turbulence even at small scales under very strong mean fields, characterizes scaling laws in small-scale whistler wave turbulence, relativistic force-free regimes, and compressible MHD turbulence, emphasizing the central role of Alfvén wave interactions across these regimes.
AI.conclusion: Alfvén waves and their interactions are the key elements driving turbulence cascades in strongly magnetized astrophysical fluids across various regimes. Strong turbulence emerges universally even under extreme conditions, and scaling relations for different regimes can be connected through the dynamics of these waves, improving the understanding of MHD turbulence in astrophysical contexts.

title: Simulations of the 21cm emission line for upcoming large-scale HI galaxy surveys
summary: Upcoming galaxy surveys with the SKA Observatory will detect neutral hydrogen (HI) across unprecedented volumes, and their scientific return will crucially depend on predictive models for HI observables. In this work, we present a framework to simulate the neutral hydrogen 21cm emission line in such large-scale HI galaxy surveys. This framework is developed as a modular layer that builds on semi-analytical models. In particular we use as bases the Galaxy Evolution and Assembly (GAEA) and L-Galaxies semi-analytical models, coupled to merger trees from the Millennium Simulation suite. We validate our framework against local Universe observations, demonstrating consistency with velocity functions, and generalised Tully-Fisher relations. Predictions based on GAEA and L-Galaxies exhibit mutual consistency despite the distinct underlying physical prescriptions. We construct mock galaxy catalogues that incorporate forward-modelled selection functions, inclination effects, and redshift broadening, reproducing the statistical distributions of HI-selected galaxies in the ALFALFA survey. Finally, we present redshift distribution forecasts for future SKA Observatory HI galaxy surveys. This framework offers a flexible tool for interpreting upcoming large-scale radio surveys and studying HI line observables as cosmological probes.

AI.tldr: Developed and validated a modular simulation framework using semi-analytical galaxy models to predict HI 21cm emission properties for upcoming SKA surveys, enabling realistic mock catalogues and cosmological forecasts based on HI observables.
AI.motivation: Upcoming SKA Observatory galaxy surveys will detect neutral hydrogen (HI) over huge cosmic volumes, requiring accurate predictive models for HI observables to maximize scientific output.
AI.method: Developed a modular simulation framework for the neutral hydrogen 21cm emission line that builds on semi-analytical models (GAEA and L-Galaxies) coupled with merger trees from the Millennium Simulation. Validated against local Universe data and incorporated effects such as selection biases, inclination, and redshift broadening to create realistic mock HI galaxy catalogues.
AI.result: The framework successfully reproduces local Universe HI velocity functions, generalised Tully-Fisher relations, and statistical distributions of HI-selected galaxies consistent with ALFALFA survey data. Predictions from both GAEA and L-Galaxies models show mutual consistency despite different physical prescriptions. Forecasts for redshift distributions in future SKA HI surveys were also produced.
AI.conclusion: This modular framework provides a robust and flexible tool to simulate and interpret HI 21cm emission in large-scale future surveys, supporting the use of HI line observables as effective cosmological probes.

title: Search for Light-Mass Fractionally Charged Particles in Space with DAMPE Experiment
summary: Free Fractionally Charged Particles (FCPs) are predicted by some theories beyond or extended to the standard model. FCPs have been widely searched for by underground and space-based experiments based on the assumption of heavy lepton-like particles. However, there is a paucity of research focusing on light-mass FCPs (LFCPs) in the sub-MeV mass range. In this work, we report the LFCPs in primary high energy cosmic rays, based on observational data from the Dark Matter Particle Explorer (DAMPE) satellite. This study utilized ten years on-orbit data of DAMPE to search for LFCPs with a charge of $\frac{2}{3}~e$. No LFCP candidate was observed. Upper flux limit of LFCPs with a mass of 0.511 MeV$/c^{2}$ and a charge of $\frac{2}{3}~e$ is determined to be $\rm 5.0 \times 10^{-11}\,cm^{-2}sr^{-1}s^{-1}$ at the $\rm 90\%$ confidence level.

AI.tldr: This paper reports a null detection of light-mass fractionally charged particles in cosmic rays using ten years of DAMPE satellite data, setting stringent upper limits on their flux.
AI.motivation: To investigate the presence of light-mass fractionally charged particles (LFCPs) in the sub-MeV mass range, which are predicted by theories beyond the standard model but have been largely unexplored due to previous focus on heavy lepton-like particles.
AI.method: Analysis of ten years of on-orbit observational data from the DAMPE satellite to search for light-mass fractionally charged particles (LFCPs) in primary high energy cosmic rays, focusing on particles with charge 2/3 e and mass around 0.511 MeV/c^2.
AI.result: No candidate LFCPs with charge 2/3 e were observed in the data; established an upper flux limit of 5.0 x 10^-11 cm^-2 sr^-1 s^-1 at 90% confidence for LFCPs with mass 0.511 MeV/c^2.
AI.conclusion: The study found no evidence of LFCPs with charge 2/3 e in the sub-MeV mass range from cosmic ray data and imposes strong upper limits on their flux, thereby constraining models predicting such particles.

title: Revisiting CPL with sign-switching density: to cross or not to cross the NECB
summary: Recent DESI DR2 BAO measurements, when combined with CMB and SNeIa data, exhibit a $3.2σ$-$3.4σ$ preference for dynamical dark energy (DE) described by the CPL-parametrized equation of state. A particularly striking feature of these reconstructions is an apparent transition from an early-time phantom-like regime to a late-time quintessence-like behavior. For positive-definite DE densities, this transition is often phrased as a crossing of the phantom divide line (PDL) at $w(a)=-1$. Allowing the DE density to become negative, however, renders the PDL (in the sense of $w(a)=-1$) non-diagnostic as a global separator: the physically meaningful criterion is instead the null energy condition boundary (NECB), $ρ_{\rm DE}+p_{\rm DE}=0$. We therefore test whether the data-driven preference for NECB-crossing in CPL reconstructions persists once alternative realizations of phantom behavior are admitted, specifically through sign-switching DE densities. To this end, we introduce and constrain two controlled phenomenological extensions of the CPL framework featuring a negative DE phase in the past. In the CPL$\to-Λ$ model, the switching epoch is tied to the CPL-inferred NECB-crossing scale factor, yielding an early-time negative cosmological-constant phase, while the post-switch evolution follows the CPL branch. In the sCPL model, the CPL equation of state is maintained at all times, while the sign switch in the energy density occurs at an independent transition redshift. We find that late-time BAO and SNeIa data drive the negative-density phase beyond their effective redshift coverage, and that this requirement is the primary driver of the inferred parameter behavior. While both models are statistically disfavored relative to the baseline CPL, admitting a negative DE phase generally reduces the significance of deviations from a cosmological constant.

AI.tldr: Study tests if allowing dark energy density to be negative in extended CPL models affects evidence for dynamical dark energy; finds negative phase pushed to unobserved epochs and that this reduces but does not fully explain deviations from a cosmological constant.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to investigate whether the observed preference for dark energy crossing the NECB (null energy condition boundary) is robust when allowing for negative dark energy densities, which could alter the physical interpretation of the phantom divide line crossing and inform the nature of dynamical dark energy.
AI.method: The authors developed two controlled phenomenological extensions of the CPL parametrization: one where the DE density switches sign at the CPL-inferred NECB-crossing scale factor (CPL→-Λ model), and another where the sign-switching occurs at an independent transition redshift (sCPL model). They constrained these models using late-time BAO and SNeIa data to assess the impact on inferred DE behavior.
AI.result: This paper analyzes recent DESI DR2 BAO data combined with CMB and SNeIa to explore the evidence for dynamical dark energy (DE) exhibiting a transition across the phantom divide line (PDL) and the physically meaningful null energy condition boundary (NECB). It introduces two extensions of the CPL-parametrized DE model allowing a negative DE density phase in the past, testing if the NECB-crossing preference persists. Statistical fits show that late-time BAO and SNeIa data push the negative DE phase beyond observed redshifts, reducing but not eliminating signs of dynamical DE and are generally disfavored compared to the standard CPL model.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating a negative dark energy density phase in phenomenological CPL extensions lessens the statistical preference for dynamical DE deviations but does not fully restore the cosmological constant model; these extensions are statistically less favored than the baseline CPL model.

title: ASKAP J005512.2-255834: A Luminous, Long-Lived Radio Transient at z = 0.1 -- an Orphan Afterglow or an off-nuclear TDE from an IMBH?
comment: This paper has been accepeted for publication in ApJ
summary: We report the discovery of a slowly evolving, extragalactic radio transient, ASKAP J005512.2--255834 (hereafter ASKAP J0055-2558), identified using the Australian SKA Pathfinder in a search for orphan afterglows associated with archival gravitational wave events. Although discovered in this context, there is no evidence that the transient is associated with any known gravitational wave event. Nonetheless, this source exhibits a 20-fold increase in flux density over $<250$ days, and it remains in a declining, detectable state more than 1000 days after the initial detection. Follow-up observations from 0.3 to 9 GHz reveal an evolving spectrum consistent with synchrotron emission. ASKAP J0055-2558 is spatially coincident with a low-mass, star-forming galaxy at redshift $z = 0.116$ ($d_{\rm L}$= 543 Mpc), placing its peak radio luminosity at $νL_ν\sim 10^{39}\,\rm erg\,s^{-1}$. Analysis of its radio light curve, inferred blastwave velocity, energetics, host galaxy properties and the absence of counterparts at other wavelengths suggest that ASKAP J0055-2558 is most consistent with either the late-time phase of an orphan long gamma-ray burst afterglow or a tidal disruption event involving an intermediate-mass black hole spatially offset from the galaxy nucleus. The radio discovery of either of these phenomena is extremely rare, with only a few or no confirmed examples to date.

AI.tldr: A rare extragalactic radio transient, ASKAP J005512.2--255834, was discovered via the Australian SKA Pathfinder with a slowly evolving synchrotron spectrum and high luminosity, likely representing an orphan long gamma-ray burst afterglow or a tidal disruption event involving an intermediate-mass black hole.
AI.motivation: Search for orphan afterglows associated with archival gravitational wave events to identify rare extragalactic radio transients.
AI.method: Utilized the Australian SKA Pathfinder to detect radio transients, followed by multi-frequency observations from 0.3 to 9 GHz to analyze the spectral evolution and synchrotron emission characteristics.
AI.result: Discovered ASKAP J005512.2--255834, a slowly evolving radio transient with a 20-fold flux increase in under 250 days, detectable over 1000 days, spatially coincident with a low-mass star-forming galaxy at redshift 0.116, exhibiting characteristics consistent with a long gamma-ray burst afterglow or a tidal disruption event involving an intermediate-mass black hole.
AI.conclusion: ASKAP J0055-2558 represents a rare radio transient, likely an orphan long gamma-ray burst afterglow or a tidal disruption event, identified through radio observations without multi-wavelength counterparts, expanding understanding of such rare phenomena.

title: AT 2024wpp: the most luminous fast-evolving optical transient linked to the merger explosion of a black-hole binary
summary: Fast blue optical transients (FBOTs) represent one of the most exotic astrophysical transients, exhibiting unusually strong emission across X-ray, optical, and radio wavelengths. Their physical origins remain highly debated, with proposed explanations ranging from stellar explosion to tidal disruption event (TDE). Here we report observations of the most luminous FBOT, AT 2024wpp whose post-peak luminosity rebrightens in X ray and becomes flattening in optical in a manner follows the decay rate characteristic of TDEs ($L_{\rm bol} \propto t^{-5/3}$). This invokes energy contribution of accretion by a central compact object, getting further corroborations from hardening of X-ray spectral index and detection of outflow inferred from the emission lines at similar phase. Detailed modeling of luminsoity evolution favors a coalesce explosion of a 34 M$_{\odot}$ Wolf-Rayet star with a 15 M$_{\odot}$ black hole (BH), demonstrating that some FBOTs may be associated with TDE of a stellar blackhole.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the luminous FBOT AT 2024wpp, showing its post-peak luminosity and spectral features align with tidal disruption event signatures, suggesting some FBOTs originate from disruptions involving stellar-mass black holes.
AI.motivation: To understand the physical origins of fast blue optical transients (FBOTs), which exhibit strong multiwavelength emission and remain highly debated, with potential explanations including stellar explosions and tidal disruption events (TDEs).
AI.method: Observations and detailed modeling of the FBOT AT 2024wpp, focusing on its post-peak luminosity evolution in X-ray and optical wavelengths, spectral analyses including the X-ray spectral index hardening and emission line diagnostics for outflows.
AI.result: The post-peak luminosity of AT 2024wpp shows rebrightening in X-rays and optical flattening that follows a decay rate characteristic of TDEs. The X-ray spectral hardening and detected outflows support energy injection from accretion by a central compact object. Modeling favors a merger explosion of a 34 M☉ Wolf-Rayet star with a 15 M☉ black hole, indicating some FBOTs may be linked to the tidal disruption of a stellar-mass black hole.
AI.conclusion: Some FBOTs, including the most luminous AT 2024wpp, can be explained by tidal disruption events involving a stellar black hole, supported by observational evidence and luminosity modeling consistent with TDE decay rates.

title: The Magnetic Filling in MAD Simulations and its Impact on the Jet in M87
summary: Magnetically arrested accretion disks (MADs) in black hole jet launching simulations are very successful in modelling low-luminosity active galactic nuclei (AGN) like M87*. The Fishbone-Moncrief torus is well established for this purpose in numerical astrophysics. The extent of the magnetic vector potential inside the torus that we coin the filling factor has not been studied before in the case of MAD simulations. We employ five 3D general relativistic magneto-hydrodynamics (GRMHD) simulations initialized with large-scale tori, that are immersed in weak, poloidal magnetic fields. To study the impact of the spatial extent of the initial magnetic field, hence the magnetic energy content in the torus, we scale it with the filling factor w.r.t. the poloidal geometric area of the mass density distribution. A common choice of the filling factor is complimented and investigated in terms of altered energetics and angular momentum transport. Further, we investigate the polarized, radiative imprints of synchrotron emission on M87 at 86 GHz, comparing them with VLBI observations. Our simulations show that elevated filling factors significantly increase the electromagnetic energy contributions and outward angular momentum transport in the jet, due to the initially increased magnetic energy-content in the torus. High magnetic fillings exhibit increased linear polarization fractions, agreeing with the observed 15$\%$ in M87*. We find the jet morphology more prone to disk-vertical flux tubes generated by MAD events. We show, that GRMHD simulations bracket the jet width measurements at the jet base in M87*. Increased magnetic filling of the torus produces jets that are noticeably brighter downstream compared to our reference models, hence, we find high fillings well suited for extended GRMHD jet models of other low-luminosity AGN, as well.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how varying the magnetic field's spatial extent inside the torus (filling factor) in GRMHD simulations of MADs affects jet energetics, polarization, and morphology, showing that higher fillings better reproduce observations of M87* and benefit modeling low-luminosity AGN jets.
AI.motivation: To study the impact of the spatial extent of the initial magnetic field (filling factor) inside the Fishbone-Moncrief torus on magnetically arrested accretion disks (MAD) simulations relevant to low-luminosity active galactic nuclei like M87*.
AI.method: Five 3D general relativistic magneto-hydrodynamics (GRMHD) simulations initialized with large-scale tori immersed in weak, poloidal magnetic fields, varying the magnetic vector potential spatial extent (filling factor) within the torus.
AI.result: Elevated filling factors increase electromagnetic energy and outward angular momentum transport in jets, raise linear polarization fractions matching observations, affect jet morphology by generating disk-vertical flux tubes, and produce jets brighter downstream, aligning well with jet width measurements at M87*'s jet base.
AI.conclusion: Increasing the magnetic filling factor in GRMHD simulations of MADs enhances jet electromagnetic energy, angular momentum transport, polarization, and brightness, suggesting high magnetic fillings are well suited for extended jet models of low-luminosity AGN such as M87*.

title: Evidence of a non-equipartition energy regime in 1803+784 Core-shift and Faraday rotation measurements from simultaneous multi-frequency polarimetric VGOS observations
comment: Published in Astron. Astrophys. (A&A) Letters, 700, L22 (2025). 6 pages, 3 figures. Published online: 20 Aug 2025
summary:
Context. Compact jets from active galactic nuclei (AGN) are commonly assumed to be in equipartition between particle and magnetic-field energy densities at the regions where the radio emission dominates at centimetre wavelengths. This assumption has significant implications for both jet physics and the accuracy of VLBI-based astrometry and geodesy.
  Aims. We tested the validity of the energy equipartition hypothesis in AGN cores at centimetre wavelengths by analysing the blazar 1803+784 using simultaneous broadband full-polarization observations with the VLBI Global Observing System (VGOS).
  Methods. We present VGOS observations of the blazar 1803+784 covering the 3-11 GHz frequency range. The data were processed using a dedicated calibration pipeline, followed by model fitting and multi-frequency imaging analysis. We measured the frequency-dependent core shift and mapped the spectral index and rotation measure (RM) across the source.
  Results. We find a core-shift power-law index of $k_r = 0.73^{+0.12}_{-0.19}$, significantly deviating from the expected equipartition value of $k_r = 1$. This indicates that either the equipartition condition or the conical jet geometry, or both, are not fulfilled in the centimetre-wavelength core region. The wide frequency coverage of VGOS also allows us to decouple the Faraday rotation of the core into an internal component (${\rm RM}_I = 121 \pm 8$ rad m$^{-2}$, produced in the core region) and an external component (${\rm RM}_E = -44 \pm 9$ rad m$^{-2}$, associated with a distant, extended medium that may also affect the polarization in downstream regions of the jet at larger scales).
  Conclusions. These results demonstrate the power of VGOS for high-fidelity simultaneous multi-frequency polarimetric studies of compact AGN jets, and underline the need to account for non-equipartition effects in both jet astrophysics and geodetic VLBI.

AI.tldr: VGOS observations of blazar 1803+784 show the cm-wavelength AGN core deviates from energy equipartition and conical jet geometry, mandating revised models for jet physics and VLBI astrometry.
AI.motivation: To test the validity of the energy equipartition hypothesis in AGN cores at centimetre wavelengths, which impacts jet physics and VLBI astrometry.
AI.method: Simultaneous broadband full-polarization VLBI observations of blazar 1803+784 using VGOS in the 3-11 GHz frequency range, followed by calibration, model fitting, multi-frequency imaging, core-shift measurement, spectral index and rotation measure mapping.
AI.result: Measured core-shift power-law index k_r=0.73(+0.12/-0.19), deviating from expected equipartition value of 1, indicating violation of equipartition and/or conical jet geometry assumptions. Decoupled Faraday rotation into internal and external components.
AI.conclusion: VGOS enables high-fidelity, simultaneous multi-frequency polarimetric studies, revealing non-equipartition conditions in AGN cores that must be considered in jet astrophysics and geodetic VLBI analyses.

title: Pulsar Discoveries from the TRAPUM UHF Survey of Fermi-LAT Sources
comment: 19 pages, 6 figures, accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: The Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) provides advantages for radio pulsar searches by enabling efficient target selection. We can confidently point radio telescopes to the positions of Fermi unidentified gamma-ray sources that have a high probability of hosting a pulsar. As part of Transients and Pulsars with MeerKAT (TRAPUM), we conducted a survey of Fermi-LAT sources using the Ultra High Frequency (UHF; 544-1088 MHz) receiver of the MeerKAT radio telescope. We observed 79 sources that were identified as pulsar-like candidates using a random forest technique from the Fermi-LAT Fourth Source Catalogue. We observed each target for 10 minutes at two separate epochs. As a result, we discovered nine new millisecond pulsars (MSPs) and six slow pulsars. Based on the radio discoveries, we also searched for gamma-ray pulsations, confirming that seven of the newly discovered MSPs are associated with Fermi-LAT sources, and performed joint radio and gamma-ray pulsar timing. Companion mass estimates and evidence of radio eclipses indicate that among the nine MSPs there are three black widows and three redbacks. Lastly, we compared the discovered pulsars in the MeerKAT UHF survey against the previous Fermi sources TRAPUM survey at L band, concluding the superiority of UHF observations in sensitivity to fainter pulsars and in detection rate than L band for finding new gamma-ray MSPs.

AI.tldr: A MeerKAT UHF survey of Fermi-LAT sources discovered 15 new pulsars, confirmed 7 gamma-ray MSP associations, and showed UHF's superior sensitivity over L band for pulsar detection.
AI.motivation: To efficiently discover new radio pulsars by targeting Fermi-LAT unidentified gamma-ray sources with a high likelihood of hosting pulsars, leveraging the improved sensitivity of the MeerKAT UHF receiver compared to previous surveys at L band.
AI.method: The study selected 79 Fermi-LAT sources classified as pulsar-like using a random forest classifier from the 4FGL catalogue. Each target was observed twice for 10 minutes using MeerKAT's UHF receiver. Radio pulse searches were conducted to detect pulsars, followed by gamma-ray pulsation searches and joint timing to confirm source associations. Companion masses and eclipses were analyzed to characterize binary systems.
AI.result: The paper reports a targeted radio pulsar survey of 79 Fermi-LAT gamma-ray sources using the MeerKAT telescope's UHF receiver, resulting in the discovery of 15 new pulsars (9 millisecond and 6 slow pulsars). Seven MSPs were confirmed through gamma-ray pulsation searches and timing analysis, with companion mass estimates identifying binary systems including black widows and redbacks. The study also demonstrates that UHF observations outperform previous L band surveys in detecting faint gamma-ray MSPs in terms of sensitivity and detection rate.
AI.conclusion: The use of the MeerKAT UHF receiver for targeted radio observations of Fermi-LAT sources is highly effective, yielding multiple new pulsar discoveries and outperforming previous L band surveys in detecting faint gamma-ray MSPs, highlighting UHF's advantage for future pulsar searches.

title: Revisiting the Geminga halo at GeV energies with Fermi-LAT data
comment: 12 pages, 7 figures. Accepted for publication in PRD
summary: Nearby pulsars within $\sim1\,{\rm kpc}$ are considered to be possible sources of 10-500 GeV cosmic-ray positron excess measured by PAMELA and AMS-02. A TeV halo around Geminga is detected by HAWC, and the measurements of its surface brightness profile indicate a slow particle diffusion surrounding the source. This result challenges the pulsar interpretation of the positron excess. The observations at GeV energies provide direct information on the electron/positron density in the GeV nebula, which can offer more direct constraints on the origin of the positron excess. Two previous works have performed analyses on the GeV emission of the pulsar halo, but focused on the energy band above 8 GeV. In this work, we use a longer dataset from the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) to re-analyze the GeV halo emission of Geminga, extending the analysis to cover the energy range of 1-1000 GeV. We find that the analysis in this wider energy range results in a low significance of the halo emission. This can be attributed to the Galactic interstellar emission model being unable to perfectly fit the background over this broader energy range, and due to the low measured halo flux at $<$ 10 GeV energies leading to a mismatch between the observation and model expectation. We also derive the spectral energy distribution of the tentative halo emission, which shows a very hard spectrum in the 1-10 GeV range.

AI.tldr: Analysis of Geminga's GeV halo emission with Fermi LAT over 1-1000 GeV shows low halo detection significance due to background modeling issues and low flux below 10 GeV, revealing a hard spectrum in 1-10 GeV but complicating the pulsar positron excess interpretation.
AI.motivation: To investigate the origin of the cosmic-ray positron excess by analyzing the GeV emission from the Geminga pulsar halo, particularly extending the energy analysis below 8 GeV where previous studies were limited.
AI.method: Using an extended dataset from the Fermi LAT to analyze the Geminga pulsar halo emission over a wide energy range (1-1000 GeV) and comparing the results with Galactic interstellar emission models to constrain the halo emission spectrum.
AI.result: The halo emission significance decreases over the extended energy range due to imperfect Galactic emission model fitting and low measured flux below 10 GeV. The tentative halo emission shows a very hard spectral energy distribution in the 1-10 GeV range.
AI.conclusion: The extended energy range analysis suggests challenges in confirming the pulsar halo emission at GeV energies, partly due to modeling limitations and low flux at lower energies, impacting the interpretation of the positron excess origin from Geminga.

title: Relativistic Dissipative Magnetohydrodynamics from the Boltzmann equation for 2-particle species gas
summary: We derive the equations of motion of relativistic magnetohydrodynamics from the Boltzmann equation using the method of moments. We consider a locally electrically neutral system composed of two particle species with opposite charges, with vanishing dipole moment or spin, so that the fluid has vanishing magnetization and polarization. We find that the dynamics of this fluid changes dramatically in the presence of a magnetic field. The shear stress tensor no longer adheres to a single differential equation; instead, it splits into three non-degenerate components, each evolving according to distinct dynamical equations. Exploring these equations in a Bjorken flow scenario, we find that for large magnetic fields, our theory predicts oscillatory behavior beyond the scope of an Israel-Stewart-like theory.

AI.tldr: Relativistic magnetohydrodynamics equations derived from Boltzmann approach reveal complex shear stress dynamics and oscillatory behavior in strong magnetic fields, beyond Israel-Stewart theory.
AI.motivation: To develop a more accurate theoretical framework for relativistic magnetohydrodynamics that accounts for effects of magnetic fields on a neutral charged fluid, overcoming limitations of existing Israel-Stewart-like theories.
AI.method: The motion equations are derived from the relativistic Boltzmann equation using the method of moments for a two-species charged fluid with no net magnetization or polarization, analyzing the resulting dynamics particularly under Bjorken flow conditions.
AI.result: The paper derives the relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) equations from the Boltzmann equation via the moment method, focusing on a locally neutral two-species charged fluid without magnetization or polarization. Key findings include the splitting of the shear stress tensor into three distinct components under a magnetic field, each governed by separate dynamic equations. Application to Bjorken flow reveals oscillatory solutions in strong magnetic fields, surpassing Israel-Stewart theory predictions.
AI.conclusion: The presence of a magnetic field fundamentally alters the fluid dynamics by splitting the shear stress tensor and inducing oscillatory behavior not captured by traditional Israel-Stewart theory, indicating the necessity of the generalized moment-derived equations for accurate description.

title: Turbulent AGN coronae as the origin of diffuse neutrinos up to PeV energies
summary: It has been shown that the turbulence acceleration in AGN coronae can account for 1-10 TeV neutrinos from some AGNs, such as the Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068. Based on this, there are attempts to explain the diffuse neutrinos observed by IceCube with the accumulated contribution from a population of AGNs, but it is found that the maximum neutrino energy is less than tens of TeV and, as a result, additional source classes are needed to explain the high-energy component above this energy. Recently, motivated by the detection of >100 TeV neutrinos from the Seyfert galaxy NGC 7469, it was shown that the turbulence acceleration in the corona can explain >100 TeV neutrinos given a larger magnetization parameter ($σ\sim 1$) in the corona, which leads to a larger maximum proton energy and a hard proton spectrum. In this paper, we extend this assumption to the population of AGNs and study whether the population of AGNs with a wide range of magnetization can explain the entire diffuse neutrinos. We find that AGN coronae could account for the diffuse neutrinos up to PeV energies if a significant fraction of AGNs have magnetization as large as $σ\sim 1-10$. This conclusion is insensitive to the shape of the magnetization parameter distribution as long as the range of the magnetization parameter is sufficiently wide and the distribution is flat towards high magnetization. Interestingly, this model can also explain the peak of the diffuse neutrino spectrum at 30 TeV.

AI.tldr: This study demonstrates that turbulence acceleration in AGN coronae, assuming a broad and sufficiently high magnetization distribution, can explain the full diffuse neutrino spectrum up to PeV energies observed by IceCube, including the 30 TeV spectral peak.
AI.motivation: To explain the diffuse neutrinos observed by IceCube, including the high-energy component above tens of TeV, and motivated by recent >100 TeV neutrino detections from Seyfert galaxies.
AI.method: Extending the turbulence acceleration model in AGN coronae with a wide range of magnetization parameters, particularly considering large magnetization (σ ~ 1-10), to the population of AGNs to calculate their contribution to diffuse neutrinos.
AI.result: The model shows that AGN coronae with a significant fraction of large magnetization can account for diffuse neutrinos up to PeV energies and explains the 30 TeV peak in the diffuse neutrino spectrum. This result is robust against different shapes of magnetization distribution if the range is sufficiently wide and flat towards high magnetization.
AI.conclusion: The population of AGNs with a wide range of magnetization, particularly with high magnetization parameters, can explain the entire diffuse neutrino spectrum observed by IceCube up to PeV energies, resolving the need for additional source classes for the high-energy component.

title: Black hole-Neutron star distinction based on long-term MAXI and Swift study of 42 low mass X-ray binaries
comment: 42 pages, 46 figures, 2 tables, Accepted for publication in Journal of Astrophysics and Astronomy (JOAA)
summary: In this study, we analysed about $\sim$13 years of publicly available data from MAXI and Swift/BAT to examine the long-term source evolution of 42 transient low-mass X-ray binaries. The sample consists of 11 confirmed black hole X-ray binaries (BHXBs), 10 black hole candidates (BHC), and 21 neutron star X-ray binaries (NSXBs). Outbursts and flaring activities studied over 13 years show that 19/21 NSXBs spend significantly longer time in the hard state (observations for which hardness ratio is $\geq$ 0.2) while 15/21 BHXB+XRC spend substantially longer time in the soft state (observations for which hardness ratio is $<$ 0.2). The frequency distribution of the hardness ratio clearly shows two distinct distributions for BHXBs and NSXBs, with their peaks separated: NSXBs prefer harder values, while BHXBs prefer softer values of hardness. Our model-independent analysis for 42 transient sources shows that statistically NSXBs do not prefer to show a canonical high soft state as observed in BHXBs. Additionally, the probability distribution of the duration of the 2-20 keV X-ray outburst is observed to peak at a significantly longer duration ($>$100 days) for BHXBs than for NSXBs (15-60 days). Our analysis shows that among candidate sources, Swift J1728.9-3613, MAXI J1535-571, MAXI J1659-152, EXO 1846-031 show a `q' diagram in the HID and prefer to align with the HID frequency distribution of BHXBs that show `q' diagram, MAXI J1305-704 and MAXI J1836-194 align with frequency distribution of black hole sources without `q' diagram while MAXI J1848-015 shows the HID distribution similar to NSXBs, indicating a neutron star accretor. Therefore, a long-term statistical study of MAXI and Swift/BAT X-ray outbursts from a large sample of transient sources may be used to distinguish BHXB from NSXB.

AI.tldr: This study uses 13 years of MAXI and Swift/BAT data to analyze 42 transient low-mass X-ray binaries, demonstrating that black hole and neutron star systems differ systematically in spectral states and outburst durations, allowing statistical classification based on hardness ratios and HID features.
AI.motivation: To investigate long-term spectral and temporal evolution of transient low-mass X-ray binaries for distinguishing black hole accretors from neutron star accretors, enhancing understanding of their accretion state behaviors and classification criteria.
AI.method: We analyzed approximately 13 years of public MAXI and Swift/BAT X-ray data from 42 transient low-mass X-ray binaries (including confirmed BHXBs, BHCs, and NSXBs), focusing on hardness ratios, outburst durations, and HID properties to compare spectral states and temporal characteristics across source types.
AI.result: NSXBs predominantly remain in harder spectral states with shorter outbursts (15-60 days), whereas BHXBs exhibit longer outbursts (>100 days) and spend more time in softer states. Distinct bimodal hardness ratio distributions separate BHXBs and NSXBs. Candidate sources show HID patterns that statistically align with either BHXB or NSXB classes, enabling classification via long-term X-ray monitoring data.
AI.conclusion: Long-term X-ray monitoring of transient low-mass X-ray binaries reveals systematic differences in spectral state preferences and outburst durations between black hole X-ray binaries (BHXBs) and neutron star X-ray binaries (NSXBs). These distinctions allow for statistical classification of candidate sources based on their hardness ratio distributions and hardness–intensity diagram (HID) behaviors.

title: Molecular bipolar outflow in SN 1987A supports the jittering-jets explosion mechanism
comment: It will be submitted in two days to allow for comments (including missing references)
summary: I examine high-quality CO and SiO molecular maps of the core-collapse supernova (CCSN) remnant SN 1987A from the literature and find that the molecular gas exhibits a bipolar structure, correlated with the visible bipolar morphology (termed the keyhole) and the bipolar morphology of the iron emission map. The keyhole has a morphology similar to that of many jet-shaped pairs of bubbles in cooling-flow clusters of galaxies and planetary nebulae. Therefore, the findings of this study, which make the bipolar structure of SN 1987A robust, strengthen the claim that a pair of energetic jets shaped the keyhole and its surroundings. According to the jittering-jets explosion mechanism (JJEM), this pair of jets was the most energetic of several pairs that exploded SN 1987A. This study adds to the accumulating evidence that the JJEM is the primary explosion mechanism of CCSNe, responsible for the majority, or even all, CCSNe.

AI.tldr: SN 1987A's molecular and visible structures show a bipolar morphology shaped by energetic jets, supporting the jittering-jets explosion mechanism as the principal cause of its explosion.
AI.motivation: To analyze molecular maps of SN 1987A to understand its morphological structure and underlying explosion mechanism.
AI.method: Examination and comparative analysis of high-quality CO and SiO molecular maps from literature alongside visible and iron emission morphologies to identify structural correlations.
AI.result: Discovery of a robust bipolar molecular structure in SN 1987A, correlated with visible bipolar features and iron emission, supporting the role of energetic jets shaping its morphology.
AI.conclusion: The bipolar morphology of SN 1987A evidences that energetic jets, as proposed by the jittering-jets explosion mechanism, played a dominant role in its explosion, suggesting JJEM may underpin most core-collapse supernovae.

title: The no-hair theorems at work in the tidal disruption event AT2020afhd
summary: Recently, the coprecession of both the accretion disk and the jet formed following the tidal disruption event associated with the optical transient AT2020afhd, driven by a supermassive black hole of almost ten million solar masses, were independently measured in both the X and radio bands, respectively, showing a periodicity of nearly 20 days over about 300 days. An analytical model of the general relativistic gravitomagnetic Lense-Thirring precession of the effective orbit of a fictitious test particle revolving about a spinning primary can explain the observed precessional features. It yields allowed regions in the system's parameter space which, as far as the hole's dimensionless spin parameter is concerned, are essentially in agreement with those obtained in the literature with general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations. The present analytical approach can be extended to include the precession due to the hole's quadrupole mass moment as well. It breaks the degeneracy in the allowed regions occurring for negative and positive values of the spin parameter when only the Lense-Thirring effect is considered. The best estimate for the hole's mass yields the range $0.185-0.215$ for the dimensionless spin parameter. Using the same strategy with the gravitomagnetic frequency for an extended disk of finite size with a parameterized power-law mass density yields to distinct, generally non-overlapping allowed regions for each value of the power-law index adopted.

AI.tldr: This study models the periodic precession observed in the accretion disk and jet after a black hole tidal disruption event using general relativistic Lense-Thirring precession, constraining the black hole spin to 0.185-0.215 and improving parameter estimates by considering quadrupole moment and extended disk effects.
AI.motivation: To explain the observed periodic precession of both the accretion disk and jet after a tidal disruption event around a supermassive black hole, and to constrain the black hole's spin parameter using an analytical relativistic precession model.
AI.method: Analytical modeling of general relativistic gravitomagnetic Lense-Thirring precession and its extension including the black hole's quadrupole mass moment; comparison with observational data in X-ray and radio bands from tidal disruption event AT2020afhd; applying parameter space analysis for the black hole's spin and mass.
AI.result: The analytical Lense-Thirring precession model successfully explains the observed 20-day periodicity over 300 days; the inclusion of the quadrupole mass moment effect resolves degeneracies in spin parameter sign; estimated black hole dimensionless spin parameter lies between 0.185 and 0.215; accounting for an extended disk with power-law mass distribution yields distinct allowed parameter regions dependent on the power-law index.
AI.conclusion: The analytical gravitomagnetic precession framework effectively explains observed data and constrains the black hole's spin; extending the model to include quadrupole moment and finite disk structure refines parameter space constraints, offering a robust tool complementary to magnetohydrodynamic simulations.
